title: CTS Worship — Unit 8: Preaching, Offering, Announcements, Invitation

blocks.en: 📖 Worship — Unit 8: Preaching, Offering, Announcements, Invitation
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Adoración — Unidad 8: Predicación, Ofrenda, Anuncios, Invitación

blocks.en: Chapala Theological Seminary, a ministry of Common Ground Fellowship | Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Seminario Teológico de Chapala, un ministerio de Common Ground Fellowship | Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: This course is drawn from the worship curriculum of Dr. Wayne Cook, who served eleven years as Professor of Pastoral Ministries and Preaching, together with the teaching of Andi Cook, who taught alongside him at the seminary. It reflects not only academic study but decades of pastoral and seminary experience.
blocks.es_reference: Este curso proviene del currículo de adoración del Dr. Wayne Cook, quien sirvió once años como Profesor de Ministerios Pastorales y Predicación, junto con la enseñanza de Andi Cook, quien enseñó a su lado en el seminario. Refleja no solo el estudio académico sino décadas de experiencia pastoral y de seminario.

blocks.en: I. Preaching as Worship
blocks.es_reference: I. La predicación como adoración

blocks.en: We come now to the elements that fill the heart of the service. The first is preaching, and we must understand from the start that preaching is itself an act of worship, not merely instruction. When the word of God is proclaimed, God speaks to His people and they respond. This is why preaching stands at the center of Protestant worship. We saw in Unit 4 that the Reformers moved the pulpit to the center of the sanctuary; that was a confession that the preached Word, not the consecrated host, is the central act of worship. The sermon is prepared from Scripture through careful study and delivered prayerfully, aimed not merely at informing the people but at moving the whole person, the mind, the heart, and the will.
blocks.es_reference: Llegamos ahora a los elementos que llenan el corazón del servicio. El primero es la predicación, y debemos entender desde el principio que la predicación es en sí misma un acto de adoración, no meramente instrucción. Cuando la palabra de Dios es proclamada, Dios habla a Su pueblo y ellos responden. Por esto la predicación está en el centro de la adoración protestante. Vimos en la Unidad 4 que los reformadores movieron el púlpito al centro del santuario; eso fue una confesión de que la Palabra predicada, no la hostia consagrada, es el acto central de la adoración. El sermón se prepara de la Escritura por medio del estudio cuidadoso y se entrega con oración, dirigido no meramente a informar al pueblo sino a mover a toda la persona, la mente, el corazón, y la voluntad.

blocks.en: II. The Offering and the Announcements
blocks.es_reference: II. La ofrenda y los anuncios

blocks.en: The offering is an act of worship and dedication, not merely fundraising. In it we dedicate our resources to God, returning to Him a portion of what He first gave us. It belongs to the mood of dedication that we studied in Unit 5, and it should be presented as worship, an act of giving to God, rather than as the collection of money to pay the bills. The way the offering is led teaches the people what it means.
blocks.es_reference: La ofrenda es un acto de adoración y dedicación, no meramente recaudación de fondos. En ella dedicamos nuestros recursos a Dios, devolviéndole una porción de lo que Él primero nos dio. Pertenece al ánimo de la dedicación que estudiamos en la Unidad 5, y debe presentarse como adoración, un acto de dar a Dios, en lugar de la colecta de dinero para pagar las cuentas. La manera en que se dirige la ofrenda enseña al pueblo lo que significa.

blocks.en: Announcements are a different matter. They should be brief and handled so that they do not detract from worship. The danger is that announcements swell to fill more time than they deserve and break the mood of worship. Recall the sober comparison from Unit 7: the reading of Scripture is far more important than the announcements, yet often takes less time. Keep announcements minimal, place them well, and consider printing them rather than letting them consume the worship hour. Do not let the trivial crowd out the eternal.
blocks.es_reference: Los anuncios son otro asunto. Deben ser breves y manejarse para que no resten de la adoración. El peligro es que los anuncios crezcan para llenar más tiempo del que merecen y rompan el ánimo de la adoración. Recuerde la comparación seria de la Unidad 7: la lectura de la Escritura es mucho más importante que los anuncios, sin embargo a menudo toma menos tiempo. Mantenga los anuncios mínimos, colóquelos bien, y considere imprimirlos en lugar de dejar que consuman la hora de adoración. No deje que lo trivial desplace lo eterno.

blocks.en: III. The Invitation: The Most Important Part
blocks.es_reference: III. La invitación: la parte más importante

blocks.en: Now we come to what I consider the most important part of the entire service: the invitation. It is the most important because it is the moment of response, the point at which people respond to what God has said. Everything else in the service has prepared the way; the invitation is the climax. Here the Spirit moves on souls and people make decisions for Christ. Preaching that issues no call to respond is incomplete; the invitation gives the hearer the chance to do something about what he has heard. The relationship between the preached word and the invitation is call and response, the word calls, and the invitation is where the answer is made.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora llegamos a lo que considero la parte más importante de todo el servicio: la invitación. Es la más importante porque es el momento de la respuesta, el punto en que la gente responde a lo que Dios ha dicho. Todo lo demás en el servicio ha preparado el camino; la invitación es el clímax. Aquí el Espíritu se mueve sobre las almas y la gente toma decisiones por Cristo. La predicación que no emite ningún llamado a responder es incompleta; la invitación da al oyente la oportunidad de hacer algo sobre lo que ha oído. La relación entre la palabra predicada y la invitación es llamado y respuesta, la palabra llama, y la invitación es donde se hace la respuesta.

blocks.en: The invitation connects directly to the mood of dedication. We noted in Unit 5 that dedication comes in two places. In the offering we dedicate our resources; in the invitation we dedicate ourselves. The invitation is the place where the worshipper gives himself back to God, and so it is the personal climax of the whole service.
blocks.es_reference: La invitación se conecta directamente con el ánimo de la dedicación. Notamos en la Unidad 5 que la dedicación viene en dos lugares. En la ofrenda dedicamos nuestros recursos; en la invitación nos dedicamos a nosotros mismos. La invitación es el lugar donde el adorador se da de vuelta a Dios, y así es el clímax personal de todo el servicio.

blocks.en: IV. Giving an Invitation Well
blocks.es_reference: IV. Dar bien una invitación

blocks.en: How is an invitation given well? First, give it clearly, so people know exactly how they may respond. Second, be sensitive to the Spirit and never rush it. I have seen an invitation last an hour and a half because the Spirit was moving, and it would have been a sin to cut it short. Third, guide people without manipulating them, no high-pressure tactics, no emotional manipulation, just a clear and patient call to respond. The Spirit, not the clock, governs the invitation. Be patient, be clear, and follow His leading.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Cómo se da bien una invitación? Primero, dela claramente, para que la gente sepa exactamente cómo puede responder. Segundo, sea sensible al Espíritu y nunca la apresure. He visto una invitación durar hora y media porque el Espíritu se movía, y habría sido un pecado cortarla. Tercero, guíe a la gente sin manipularla, sin tácticas de alta presión, sin manipulación emocional, solo un llamado claro y paciente a responder. El Espíritu, no el reloj, gobierna la invitación. Sea paciente, sea claro, y siga Su dirección.

blocks.en: Each of these elements has its proper place in the flow of the service. Preaching proclaims the word and moves the people; the offering dedicates their resources; the announcements stay brief and out of the way; and the invitation forms the climax of response. The preacher's task is to guard the service so that the lesser elements never crowd out the most important parts, the word preached and the response given. Protect what matters most.
blocks.es_reference: Cada uno de estos elementos tiene su lugar apropiado en el flujo del servicio. La predicación proclama la palabra y mueve al pueblo; la ofrenda dedica sus recursos; los anuncios permanecen breves y fuera del camino; y la invitación forma el clímax de la respuesta. La tarea del predicador es guardar el servicio para que los elementos menores nunca desplacen las partes más importantes, la palabra predicada y la respuesta dada. Proteja lo que más importa.

fill.prompt: Preaching is itself an act of ____, not merely instruction.

sa.prompt: Explain why preaching is itself an act of worship, not merely instruction.
sa.model: Preaching is itself an act of worship, not merely instruction, because when the word of God is proclaimed, God speaks to His people and they respond — this is why the Reformers moved the pulpit to the center of the sanctuary, confessing that the preached Word, not the consecrated host, is the central act of worship. A sermon aims not merely at informing the people but at moving the whole person, the mind, the heart, and the will, which is itself worship in motion.

sa.prompt: Explain the offering as an act of worship and dedication, not merely fundraising.
sa.model: The offering is an act of worship and dedication, not merely fundraising, because in it we dedicate our resources to God, returning to Him a portion of what He first gave us. It belongs to the mood of dedication studied in Unit 5, and it should be presented as worship, an act of giving to God, rather than as the collection of money to pay the bills — the way it is led teaches the people what it truly means.

sa.prompt: How should announcements be handled so they do not detract from worship?
sa.model: Announcements should be handled so they do not detract from worship by keeping them brief and placed well within the service, since the danger is that they swell to fill more time than they deserve and break the mood of worship. The reading of Scripture is far more important than the announcements, yet often takes less time — so leaders should keep announcements minimal, perhaps even printed, rather than letting them consume the worship hour.

sa.prompt: Why does Wayne consider the invitation the most important part of the service?
sa.model: Wayne considers the invitation the most important part of the service because it is the moment of response, the point at which people respond to what God has said, and everything else in the service has prepared the way for it. Here the Spirit moves on souls and people make decisions for Christ — preaching that issues no call to respond is incomplete, since the invitation gives the hearer the chance to actually act on what he has heard.

sa.prompt: Explain how the invitation connects to the mood of dedication.
sa.model: The invitation connects to the mood of dedication because dedication comes in two places: in the offering we dedicate our resources, and in the invitation we dedicate ourselves. The invitation is where the worshipper gives himself back to God, making it the personal climax of the whole service, parallel to but distinct from the material dedication of the offering.

sa.prompt: What are some practical guidelines for giving an invitation well?
sa.model: Practical guidelines for giving an invitation well include: give it clearly, so people know exactly how they may respond; be sensitive to the Spirit and never rush it, even letting it run long if the Spirit is clearly moving; and guide people without manipulating them, using no high-pressure tactics or emotional manipulation, only a clear and patient call to respond, since the Spirit, not the clock, should govern the invitation.

sa.prompt: How should the sermon be prepared and delivered as part of worship?
sa.model: The sermon should be prepared from Scripture through careful study, grounding it in the actual meaning of the text rather than personal opinion, and delivered prayerfully, depending on the Spirit rather than mere technique. It should be aimed not merely at informing the people but at moving the whole person — the mind, the heart, and the will — so that preaching becomes worship rather than a lecture.

sa.prompt: Explain the relationship between the preached word and the response of the invitation.
sa.model: The relationship between the preached word and the invitation is call and response — the word calls, and the invitation is where the answer is made. Preaching prepares and moves the hearer, and the invitation gives that hearer the concrete opportunity to act on what has been heard, so the two belong together as a single movement rather than as separate, unrelated parts of the service.

sa.prompt: How do preaching, offering, announcements, and invitation each fit the flow of the service?
sa.model: Preaching proclaims the word and moves the people; the offering dedicates their material resources; the announcements stay brief and out of the way so they do not steal time from worship; and the invitation forms the climax of personal response. Each has a distinct place and purpose in the flow of the service, moving from proclamation, through dedication of resources, to the personal climax of self-dedication.

sa.prompt: Why must the preacher guard against letting lesser elements crowd out the most important parts of worship?
sa.model: The preacher must guard against lesser elements crowding out the most important parts of worship because time and attention are limited, and every minute given to announcements or trivial matters is a minute taken from the preached word and the invitation, which carry the greatest spiritual weight of the service. Protecting what matters most means the preacher must actively manage the service's proportions rather than letting them drift.
